Topic T1 · First Impression

Where You'd Find It

What You'd Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item B1 is a small stainless socket cap screw with two features you can spot before you ever read the print: the yellow-striped thread locking patch, and the matte black finish.

As received: black oxide finish, hex socket head, and the yellow adhesive patch on the threads.
The same head and thread geometry before finishing — socket cap head, knurled head, machine screw thread.

Socket Cap Head — internal hex drive, cylindrical head profile, smaller diameter than most machine screw heads so it fits into counterbored holes.

Knurled Head — knurling on the head, added at the discretion of the manufacturer, allows the end user to make fingertip adjustments.

Machine Screw Thread — coarse, fully threaded to the head.

Black Oxide — a matte-black conversion coating finish over stainless steel.

Yellow Scotch-Grip — pre-applied adhesive patch on the thread. The adhesive activates on assembly, creating a strong bond between the external thread and the internal thread of the nut or tapped hole, which keeps the parts from loosening in vibration.

Tap an orange dot to see what that feature is.

  • Socket Cap Head — internal hex drive, cylindrical head profile, smaller diameter than most machine screw heads so it fits into counterbored holes.

  • Yellow Scotch-Grip — pre-applied adhesive patch on the thread. The adhesive activates on assembly, creating a strong bond between the external thread and the internal thread of the nut or tapped hole, which keeps the parts from loosening in vibration.

Topic T4 · Material Selection

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

The "S" in .4C16MSCSNB/SY calls out the base material. Here's what that grade actually means on the shop floor.

Requirement

Material: 18-8 (A2) stainless steel · Material grade: A2-50 or A2-70

What “18-8” Means

18-8 is an American term for a common grade of stainless steel containing 18% chromium and 8% nickel.

What A2-50 / A2-70 Mean

A2 is the 18-8 (type 304) stainless family. The number is the strength class — the minimum tensile strength in MPa divided by 10 (A2-50 ≈ 500 MPa, A2-70 ≈ 700 MPa).

Equivalent Grade

Equivalent to type 304 stainless steel.

Corrosion Resistance

Good corrosion resistance in typical service environments.

Strength

Medium strength — lower than alloy steel grades, which is the usual trade-off for corrosion resistance.

Why It Matters

18-8 is the default stainless callout across most of SBS's fastener line, which keeps sourcing and lead times predictable.

SBS's own materials cross-reference — the same 304 stainless steel under every country's standard (DIN 1.4301, JIS SUS304, ASTM/UNS S30400, and more). Try the Material Conversion tool ↗

Topic T5 · Surface Treatment

Nova 34 Black Oxide

The "NB" in the part number calls out this specific finish process.

Requirement

With Nova 34 Black Oxide.

Typical Call-Out

Black Oxide per MIL 13924D Class 4 Type Nova 34.MIL-DTL-13924D is the U.S. military spec that governs this finishing process.

Item B1 after the black oxide stage — the matte-black finish (adhesive patch not yet applied).

Meaning

Used on stainless steel fasteners. MIL-DTL-13924D (§3.9) only requires Class 4 black oxide on 300-series stainless to show no signs of corrosion after 96 hours of salt spray — not as good as passivated stainless steel. Salt Spray Test performance is therefore reference only: black oxide is not primarily a corrosion-resistance coating on stainless.

Black oxide converts the surface without adding meaningful thickness — dimensions stay in tolerance.
Plain vs. Black Oxide
Same part, same dimensions — untreated (left) and black oxide coated (right).

What Changes — and What Doesn't

  1. Plain (untreated): bright, reflective silver metal surface.
  2. Black oxide: a uniform, deep matte-black, low-glare surface.
  3. Unchanged: size, shape and thread fit — it is a conversion coating, not a plated layer.
What Black Oxide Actually Is
  • A chemical conversion process that turns stainless steel from shiny silver to a deep matte black.
  • Because it is a conversion coating (the surface itself is converted, not plated on top), it does not change the part’s dimensions or thread tolerance.
  • Forms an ultra-thin oxide layer — typically less than 1 micron thick.
  • Provides light corrosion resistance, reduced glare, and better lubricity when sealed with oil.
    • Why Black Oxide Is Used — and Where You See It

    Camouflage

    Common in military and tactical hardware to minimize reflections from sunlight or infrared light.

    Tactical & military gear: dark, low-glare hardware, such as on helmets, minimizes reflections.

    Aesthetics

    A uniform, professional, low-glare appearance preferred across many industries.

    Hardware: screws, nuts, bushings, snap rings and springs are commonly black oxide finished.

    Topic T6 · Extra Thread Locking Treatment

    The Yellow Scotch-Grip Patch

    The "/SY" suffix calls out a pre-applied adhesive patch on the threads — and a live supplier deviation worth knowing about.

    Requirement

    With Yellow Scotch-Grip 3M 2353Y, or Red ND Microspheres 593S (as per global BRP deviation), per IFI 525.BRP: a customer of SBS's (Bombardier Recreational Products). IFI 525: the industry standard for this type of thread patch.

    (1) 3M Scotch-Grip 2353Y

    Yellow color. The original, standard callout.

    (2) ND 593S Microspheres

    Red color. Accepted as a global BRP deviation.

    Why the Deviation Exists Active Deviation

    3M discontinued Scotch-Grip 2353Y. SBS temporarily accepts the global BRP deviation to substitute ND 593S Microspheres Red in its place.

    How a Thread Locker Stops Vibrational Loosening

    1. The problem. Vibration makes the mating threads slip sideways by tiny amounts. Each slip lets the screw turn back a little, clamp load drops, and the joint works loose.
    2. The patch activates on assembly. As the screw is driven in, the pre-applied adhesive is crushed between the external and internal threads and fills the gap.
    3. The bond holds. Once cured, the adhesive bonds the threads together and resists turning, so the fastener keeps its clamp load under vibration.
    SBS's own Pre-Applied Patches guide, covering nylon patches and thread lockers. Explore Pre-Applied Patches and Adhesives ↗
    With vs. Without a Locking Patch
    Top: a standard threaded fastener. Bottom: the thread locker fills the gaps (click to enlarge).

    Without a Locking Patch

    Usage — a standard threaded fastener: only the machined thread fit holds the joint.

    Effectiveness — gaps remain between the threads, so vibration lets them slip, the screw backs off, clamp load drops and the joint can work loose.

    With a Locking Patch (/SY)

    Usage — the patch is pre-applied to the threads and activates as the screw is driven in, with no separate locker to apply at assembly.

    Effectiveness — the adhesive fills the gaps and, once cured, bonds the threads and resists turning, so the fastener keeps its clamp load under vibration.

    Forest City Technologies' own certification for a real production lot — 13,063 pieces, patched with the original 3M 2353Y Yellow adhesive.

    This patch is the last step added to the part — see who applies it in .

    Reference

    Glossary

    Every code, acronym, and standard used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term's "jump" button to see it in context.

    18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

    A common grade of stainless steel, roughly equivalent to type 304. "18-8" is the American term for stainless steel with 18% chromium and 8% nickel. The material grade of the fastener is A2-50 or A2-70. It's the default stainless callout across most of SBS's fastener line.

    Black Oxide

    A chemical conversion process that turns a stainless steel surface from shiny silver to a deep matte black, without adding meaningful thickness.

    BRP

    Bombardier Recreational Products — one of SBS's customers. A "BRP deviation" is a substitution approved specifically for their orders, not a change to the part in general.

    DIN 912 / ISO 4762

    The German and international standards that define hex socket head cap screws — the head shape, drive, and dimensions this part is built to.

    FCT (Forest City Technologies)

    The supplier who applies the pre-applied adhesive thread patch — the last step in this part's manufacturing chain.

    IFI 525

    Metric Adhesive Coated Prevailing-Torque Screws — the Industrial Fasteners Institute standard covering pre-applied thread-locking patches like the one on this part.

    MIL-DTL-13924D

    The U.S. military specification that governs the black oxide finishing process used on this part, including how it's tested.

    Nova 34

    The specific black oxide process name (a Class 4 alkaline oxidizing process) used to finish this part.

    PPAP

    Production Part Approval Process — the documentation package a supplier submits to prove its process can reliably make a part to print before full production begins.

    PROP 65

    A California law requiring a warning label on products containing certain chemicals above a set threshold. "Compliant" here means the part doesn't trigger that warning.

    PSW (Part Submission Warrant)

    The signed cover document of a PPAP package — the formal sign-off that a part is approved for production.

    REACH

    A European Union regulation restricting hazardous chemicals in manufactured goods — a separate compliance check from RoHS, covering a broader list of substances.

    RoHS

    Restriction of Hazardous Substances — an EU rule limiting materials like lead and mercury in manufactured parts.

    Scotch-Grip

    The brand name of the yellow adhesive thread-locking patch pre-applied to this part's threads.

    VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)

    A bin system where SBS manages and restocks parts directly at the customer's location. This training module is named after Item B1's cell on the VMI bin card.
